summary.statement: Brands handle reorders through Faire (marketplace or Faire Direct at 0% commission), by email, or on their own password-protected Shopify wholesale site, sometimes with a discount for ordering direct.
Money cost on Faire is about 17-18% of each marketplace reorder (15% commission plus processing).
Time cost is real enough that brands hire coordinators to enter wholesale orders across Shopify B2B, Faire and FashionGo and to manage reordering; no hours figure was found.
One DTC finance analysis estimates boutiques reorder once or twice a year, a 20-35% year-one reorder rate.
No evidence found on the share of a brand's wholesale revenue that comes from reorders.
Brands stay on Faire for reorders because retailers like its convenience, breadth and terms, even shops the brand found itself.
Faire's commission funds Net 60 terms that makers often can't offer themselves.
Faire's terms forbid moving stockists Faire sourced off-platform to save commission, and brands don't get those retailers' contact details.
Makers call the fee high but feel dependent on Faire; some accept it as an advertising substitute.
For brand-sourced retailers the commission problem is already solved by Faire Direct (0%).
In the small brands found, the owner or founder runs the business (e.g. a one-person brand, an owner-operated workshop), so the owner is the likely buyer.
No evidence found on budgets for wholesale tools; a flat-fee wholesale marketplace charges $150/month as a reference point.
Retailers cite Faire's payment terms as a reason they like ordering there.
Pre-filled reorder drafts are already offered by 2026 Shopify apps, but they have no reviews, so retailer and brand uptake is unknown.
No evidence found on how stockists value case-pack rules in reorders.
Native Shopify B2B on all paid plans since April 2026 covers catalogs, payment terms and volume pricing, and commentators say it made many B2B apps redundant.
Vendors say native B2B still lacks rep ordering and quoting, the gap apps like SparkLayer and Brandboom target.
No brand-side reviews of SparkLayer or Wholesale Club were fetched; strengths and weaknesses here come from vendor pages.
Practices vary: some brands extend Net 30 on direct reorders themselves, others require prepayment for direct orders.
Native Shopify B2B now offers Net 30/60 at checkout, and independent net-terms providers such as Resolve exist.
Faire's Net 60 is a retailer draw that individual makers often can't match.
